summary: Slot glitching and prefetch throttling during dedicated autoscale window causing p95/p99 throughput regressions
description: Issue summary: During the scheduled autoscale warm-up window for Polaris AI's dedicated pool (prod | us-west) we observed repeated short-lived throughput collapses (p95 and p99) for long-context streaming workloads. Impact: Customer-facing latency regressions and request queueing leading to dropped streams and client retries. Estimated customer impact: 8-12% of requests for the affected tenant experienced >=3x p99 latency increase during the window on 2026-03-10.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer tenant Polaris AI sends sustained long-context streaming traffic to dedicated pool between 09:30-10:15 UTC. 2) Autoscaler triggers scale-up from 6->9 GPU slots (incremental warm-up). 3) Observe serving-runtime logs and scheduler metrics. 4) Observe request queue growth and repeated per-slot 'prefetch-throttle' warnings and 'slot-lock' jitter. Expected: Smooth capacity increase with stable per-slot throughput. Observed: transient slot starvations and interleaved prefetch backpressure causing serialization of short and long streams.

comments: 2026-03-10 - Support (Ava): Customer reported repeated client-side stream resets during autoscale warm-up window; opened ticket and flagged as P1 due to customer SLA breach.

2026-03-10 - Oncall SRE (Liam): Correlated serving-runtime 'prefetch_throttle' warnings with autoscaler scale events. Initial hypothesis: prefetch/backpressure on KV cache plus slow GPU attach latency causing slot serialization.
2026-03-10 - Customer (Polaris AO): We see spikes in request latency and increased retries starting around 09:36 UTC. The pattern aligns with your reported scale-ups. Logs attached from client side.

2026-03-11 - Eng (Rohit Gupta): Replayed traffic in staging; reproduced slot_lock_timeout when attaching GPUs under heavy long-context streaming. Observed NVMe prefetch queue saturation and per-slot mutex hold spikes.

2026-03-12 - Autoscaler Team (Maya): Noted that the autoscaler issued two rapid incremental attachments; we have a tentative mitigation to add a 30s attach-stagger and postpone KV-prefetch during warm-up.

2026-03-12 - Support (Liam): Proposed customer workaround: schedule warmups during off-peak hours or switch to pinned-reserve while we test fix. Customer prefers patching platform first; request expedited rollout.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: KV cache prefetching continues aggressively during scale-up; newly attached GPUs contend on NVMe, causing per-slot I/O stalls and mutex holds -> serialized batches and higher p99.

Hypothesis B: Autoscaler attaches multiple GPUs in quick succession without staggering; provisioning latency (4s-6s) plus scheduler bank-backoff causes allocation delays that amplify queueing for surviving slots.
Staging repro: Synthetic long-stream flood reproduced slot_lock_timeout at ~80% sustained load when GPUs attached within <15s intervals.
Telemetry: per-slot prefetch queue length peaked at 12 (threshold 8). NVMe write latency increased from median 2ms -> 35ms during attach events.

Cross-tenant signals: No evidence of another noisy tenant in the same pool at the time; noisy-neighbor metrics negative. Root appears tied to attach-time behaviors and prefetch settings for new allocations.
Related: linked issue SUP-631210 documented similar attach-latency patterns but attributed to background checkpoint writer; here background writer not active for this pool.
Mitigation experiments: Disabling prefetch for new slots during warm-up eliminated slot_lock timeouts in staging; adding 30s attach-stagger reduced NVMe latency peaks.

Risk assessment: Disabling prefetch may increase cold-start token costs slightly but reduces customer-facing errors during scale events. Attach-stagger delays peak provisioning but smooths throughput.

Proposed short-term mitigation: platform patch to suspend aggressive KV-prefetch for newly attached GPUs for first 60s + autoscaler attach-stagger of 30s. Long-term: dynamic prefetch throttling based on NVMe latency and active inflight counts.
resolution: Workaround applied: autoscaler team deployed attach-stagger (30s) to dedicated pools and serving-runtime patch to suppress KV-prefetch for newly attached GPUs for 60s. Deployment rolled to prod us-west at 2026-03-12T03:20Z. Post-deploy monitoring shows p99 latency for Polaris AI returned to baseline within one autoscale window and no further slot_lock_timeouts observed. Follow-ups: (1) telemetry alert for prefetch queue depth to trigger autoscaler pacing, (2) engineering story to implement adaptive prefetch throttle tied to NVMe latency (tracked in ENG backlog), (3) customer notified and agreed to re-open if regressions continue. Ticket transitioned to "Waiting on Customer" for final confirmation before Close.
